subject: Novapharma: operations evidence package + TTL carveout playbook
messages:
From: Anna Klein <anna.klein@novapharma.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: security@novapharma.com
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Novapharma - evidence request: tenant-specific log TTL + deletion proof

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this. We're running a SIG/CAIQ deep-dive ahead of procurement and have a couple of requests specific to our tenant that are blocking our control owner. We need clarity and sample evidence for two items:

1) Tenant-scoped log retention exception (Novapharma tenant ID: nov-pharma-prod-12): our legal team requested a 180-day forensic log hold for encrypted application traces for a 3-month pilot window. We need to understand what change you would make to the runtime/config to implement a tenant TTL override and what approvals kick in (product/legal).

2) Proof of deletion and chain-of-custody: for any previously-held logs, we need a demonstrable deletion manifest (timestamps, object keys, operator id) and a redacted sample export we can inspect.

Deliverables requested: lifecycle policy text for object stores, a short playbook on steps to grant a tenant carveout and revoke it, and one redacted sample manifest plus a screenshot that shows the deletion event from the audit trail (can be obfuscated for PII). Please provide estimated lead time — we need this for our SOC 2 / SIG evidence packet.

I've attached the SIG spreadsheet with the specific question rows flagged (novapharma_SIG_questions.xlsx). Can you confirm you received, and whether Redwood can produce the materials without full SLA change?

Thanks,
Anna Klein
Security Manager, Novapharma
security@novapharma.com

[Attachment: novapharma_SIG_questions.xlsx]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Anna Klein <anna.klein@novapharma.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Novapharma - evidence request: tenant-specific log TTL + deletion proof

Anna — thanks for the detail and the spreadsheet. We can produce the artifacts you listed; quick clarifying questions before we assemble the package:

• Confirm the exact tenant namespace (you listed nov-pharma-prod-12) and whether this applies to only the production compute plane or also to sandbox/test tenants.

• For the 180-day forensic hold: is this an inbound requirement for ingestion-level traces only, or do you also need application-level debug logs emitted by customer code?

• Do you require signatures/attestation from Redwood legal on the carveout (DocuSign), or is an internal sign-off plus a signed addendum acceptable?

Planned deliverables from our side (subject to your answers):
- S3 lifecycle policy and retention config for the tenant scope (text file).
- Redacted sample deletion manifest (object keys, deletion timestamps, operator id).
- Short playbook (steps + approval chain) describing how we implement a tenant TTL override and how it is revoked.
- A screenshot/export of the audit trail showing deletion events (PII redacted).

We'll need to route the tenant TTL carveout through product + legal. Neha (cc'd) will coordinate the evidence extraction and redaction, and Marissa will coordinate timing and CS communications.

Target timeline: draft package in 5 business days after we get your tenant confirmation and scope. If you can sign an exception addendum, we can reduce to ~3 business days.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0183

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: playbook + redaction approach for Novapharma TTL carveout

Folks — following Tessa's note, here's the proposed internal playbook we should present as the deliverable (concise bullets we can drop into the customer playbook):

1) Intake and scope validation (CS + Security): confirm tenant namespaces and whether non-prod is included.
2) Legal review: exception addendum template (DocuSign). Required for any retention override > 90 days.
3) Product change: create a tenant-scoped TTL override flag in the configuration service (behind a feature gate) that appends a lifecycle rule with PreserveUntil=180d for the tenant's objects. This is an operational toggle; we will not modify global defaults.
4) Evidence extraction: a) export of the lifecycle rule (s3-lifecycle-policy.txt), b) redacted deletion manifest (redacted-retention-sample.csv), c) audit log snapshot showing operator and timestamp (deletion-manifest-sample.jsonl).
4a) Redaction: mask user PII, replace object keys with stable pseudonyms, and include a mapping file internally for chains of custody.
5) Revoke process: same flow in reverse; revoke TTL via feature flag revert + signed confirmation email from legal that the exception is closed.

Estimated effort: evidence extraction + redaction = 3 business days (assuming tenant confirm). Product/legal path for addendum = up to 7 business days if signatures required.

I will prepare the sample manifest and lifecycle text today and attach to Tessa's reply. Marissa — once we have the addendum, can your team confirm scheduled windows for the config change?

Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: s3-lifecycle-policy.txt, redacted-retention-sample.csv, deletion-manifest-sample.jsonl]

From: Anna Klein <anna.klein@novapharma.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Can you include the S3 lifecycle policy text plus the redacted manifest and the audit snapshot in the package? I've started an internal tracker (see HubSpot link) and attached an initial DocuSign envelope for the addendum.
